Kindoki
Kindoki
is thought by its believers to be a kind of
witchcraft
or
possession
by evil spirits.
[
1
]
In the
Democratic Republic of the Congo
(DRC) and among
Congolese immigrants
in
Europe
, this belief is responsible for acts of
child abandonment
and
ritual abuse
of adults and children who were thought to have fallen victim to
kindoki
.
Children who are perceived to be possessed by
kindoki
are subjected to
exorcisms
that include beatings, starvation, and submersion in water.
[
1
]
The non-profit group
Save the Children
estimates that 70% of the roughly 15,000 street children in
Kinshasa
, the capital of the DRC, were kicked out of their homes after being accused of witchcraft.
The majority of witchcraft accusations come from traditional
shamans
. Some Christian preachers, however, have acted as consultants, by pointing out supposedly possessed children and carrying out "exorcisms".
